faqs.question: What size are WhatsApp stickers?
faqs.answer: Exactly 512 x 512 pixels, saved as WebP. WhatsApp's own sticker documentation, last updated 17 April 2025, also caps a static sticker at 100 KB and an animated one at 500 KB.

faqs.question: How do I add a Ganesh Chaturthi sticker pack to WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Packs come from outside WhatsApp - a sticker app or an add-to-WhatsApp link - and you add them one at a time. WhatsApp specifically tells developers not to build an 'add all packs' button, so there is no bulk shortcut.

faqs.question: Can I make my own Ganesh Chaturthi sticker?
faqs.answer: Yes. WhatsApp shipped a sticker creation and editing feature in March 2024, so you can crop your own photo into the 512-pixel square inside the app. It still will not hold a name or a sentence legibly.

faqs.question: How many stickers can one pack have?
faqs.answer: Between 3 and 30. That minimum is why nobody ever sends you a single sticker, and one sticker app can hold up to 10 separate packs.

faqs.question: Is it rude to reply to a Ganesh Chaturthi wish with just a sticker?
faqs.answer: No, and the research suggests that is what stickers are for. Reviewing the literature in Language@Internet, Ashley Dainas records that stickers can work as complete conversational turns, so a sticker is a whole reply rather than a shrug.

faqs.question: Where can I download a Ganesh Chaturthi video status?
faqs.answer: This guide will not point you at one. Almost every site ranking for that query redistributes footage without saying where it came from, and reposting someone else's film is their copyright, not yours. Shoot ten seconds of your own mandap instead.

faqs.question: Why do my Ganesh Chaturthi stickers look blurry?
faqs.answer: Because a static sticker has to fit under 100 KB at 512 x 512 pixels. Whoever made the pack compressed it to hit that ceiling, and heavy compression on a detailed idol shows.

faqs.question: Can a WhatsApp sticker have someone's name on it?
faqs.answer: Not readably. A 512-pixel square under 100 KB has no room for text at a legible size, which is exactly why a downloaded pack is identical for everyone who installed it.

faqs.question: Do animated Ganesh Chaturthi stickers work on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Yes, within limits: an animated sticker must stay under 500 KB and run no longer than 10 seconds in total. A pack is either all animated or all static, never a mix of the two.

faqs.question: When should I send Ganesh Chaturthi wishes in 2026?
faqs.answer: Ganesh Chaturthi is Monday 14 September 2026 and visarjan is Friday 25 September. On the one festival SubhSandesh measured properly - Raksha Bandhan, n = 89 - 49.4% of pages were built on the day itself, so the morning is normal rather than late.

faqs.question: Is a sticker better than a forwarded image?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. A sticker is transparent, small and reads as a reply, while a forwarded image reads as something you passed along. Neither one carries the recipient's name.

faqs.question: Do I need a third-party app to get sticker packs?
faqs.answer: For somebody else's artwork, usually yes - packs are distributed as separate apps or add-to-WhatsApp links. This guide does not name or recommend any specific one, because the listings ranking for this query are unvetted.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Happy Ganesh Chaturthi Stickers for WhatsApp: A Reply, Not a Wish

Happy Ganesh Chaturthi stickers for WhatsApp are 512 × 512 pixel WebP files under 100 KB, in packs of 3 to 30 — WhatsApp's own published limits, last updated 17 April 2025. That ceiling is the whole story. A sticker holds a face and maybe two words; it cannot hold a name, a date or a sentence. So a sticker works as a **reply** — you tap it back when someone wishes you first — not as the wish itself. For the wish you send, the counterpart is a page carrying their name: across **3,894** SubhSandesh pages built since 12 March 2026, each is opened **11.8** times on average, and **49.6%** of those opens happen on a phone (22,817 of 46,005 views, measured 2026-09-09). Below: what the format forbids, what the research says, and when a sticker is the better call.

## What a WhatsApp sticker is: 512 x 512 pixels, WebP, under 100 KB

A WhatsApp sticker is a square image with a transparent background, exactly 512 × 512 pixels, saved in WebP, sent from the sticker tray instead of typed. It is neither a photo nor a GIF, and the file enforces that: WhatsApp's [own sticker documentation for developers](https://github.com/WhatsApp/stickers/blob/main/Android/README.md), last updated 17 April 2025, caps a static sticker at 100 KB and an animated one at 500 KB and 10 seconds.

Almost everything odd about stickers follows from those numbers. 100 KB is a fraction of a phone photo, so stickers are drawn, not photographed — hence every Ganesh sticker you have seen is an illustration.

A pack must hold 3 to 30 stickers, so nobody ships a single one. An app can carry up to 10 packs, and WhatsApp tells developers not to build an "add all packs" button — hence one tap per pack. Packs are all static or all animated, never mixed.

## Why a sticker is a reply and not a wish

The key finding is about turns. Reviewing the literature in *Language@Internet*, Ashley Dainas records that stickers ["can serve as turn construction units (TCUs), or complete turns"](https://scholarworks.iu.edu/journals/index.php/li/article/view/40793) and can signal the start or end of a conversation. A sticker is a whole move, not decoration on one.

What kind of move? In Herring and Dainas's Facebook sample, emotional reaction was among the commonest functions of stickers, and stickers were "mentioned" rather than "used" — the point being the sticker itself, not what it depicted. Dolot and Opina found the same across ten Facebook group chats of young Filipino users: [the sticker was the least-used graphicon they coded](https://al-kindipublisher.com/index.php/ijllt/article/view/1772), most often as "mention".

The largest published corpus of custom WhatsApp stickers agrees. Linares Bernabéu and Yus coded [598 user-generated stickers from Spanish WhatsApp conversations](https://www.jbe-platform.com/content/journals/10.1075/prag.24063.lin) — 496 multimodal, 102 text-only.

**56.9%** clarified or emphasised the sender's intention, **24.67%** did the work of the message itself, **18.41%** worked on the recipient's inference. Only the abstract was readable from here, so those figures are all I claim from it.

Note the majority function: marking *how* you meant something presupposes something already said — the grammar of a response, and why a sticker closes a thread rather than opening one.

## Five things people send on Ganesh Chaturthi, and what each carries

Four questions each time: what it is, who it suits, what it takes, what it cannot carry.

### 1. A downloaded sticker pack (3 to 30 stickers)

**What it is:** somebody else's illustrations, installed via a third-party app or an add-to-WhatsApp link. **Who it suits:** anyone replying to many wishes, warmly and fast. **What it takes:** a minute. **What it cannot carry:** you. The file is byte-identical for everyone with that pack, which is why nine people send the same laddoo-Ganesha in one morning. No app is named here: these listings are unvetted.

### 2. A sticker you make in WhatsApp

**What it is:** WhatsApp shipped sticker creation and editing in March 2024, per Dainas's review, so you can cut your own image to the 512 × 512 WebP shape in-app. **Who it suits:** anyone with a good photo of their mandap. **What it takes:** two or three minutes. **What it cannot carry:** a name, a date, or text of any length — a 512-pixel square under 100 KB holds no sentence legibly.

### 3. A festival video clip for your status

**What it is:** a short clip posted to your status or forwarded on. **Who it suits:** almost nobody — nearly every result ranking for the video-status query is a redistribution site that never says where its footage came from, so this guide names none and gives no download steps. Reposting someone's film is their copyright, not yours. **What it cannot carry:** provenance. If a video should be the wish, shoot it: the [Watch page template](https://subhsandesh.in/watch) gives one video you made a real player, chapters and a pinned comment.

### 4. A photo of your own mandap

**What it is:** a plain image message, or your display picture for the ten days to 25 September. **Who it suits:** family groups, where the decoration is the news. **What it takes:** nothing. **What it cannot carry:** a message addressed to one person — a photo sent to forty is a broadcast, read as one.

### 5. A page they perform themselves

**What it is:** the opposite of a downloaded pack. On the [Ganesh Chaturthi page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) the recipient offers the durva, kumkum, flowers and modak themselves, while the aarti thali circles to *Karpur Gauram*. **Who it suits:** the few whose wish should be from you specifically — a grandparent, an in-law, someone you missed this year. **What it takes:** a few minutes, with a [step-by-step guide](https://subhsandesh.in/guides/happy-ganesh-chaturthi). **What it cannot carry:** the casualness of a sticker — a link asks to be opened, not an ask to make forty times.

## The five compared: 100 KB against no pixel cap

The last column is SubhSandesh's own data, measured 2026-09-09 across all 3,894 pages.

| What you send | Hard limit, and who sets it | Carries their name | What SubhSandesh has measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Downloaded sticker pack | 512 × 512 WebP, ≤ 100 KB each, 3–30 per pack (WhatsApp, 17 Apr 2025) | No | Not measurable — no link |
| Sticker made in WhatsApp | Same 512 × 512 and 100 KB ceiling; static-only packs | No | Not measurable |
| Forwarded festival clip | Animated stickers stop at 500 KB and 10 s; a forwarded clip is plain media | No | Not measurable |
| Photo of your own mandap | Plain image message; no sticker spec | No | Not measurable |
| A page they perform themselves | No pixel or byte cap — it is a web page | Yes | 11.8 opens per page; 49.6% of opens on a phone; 96.0% of started pages shared (3,737 of 3,894) |

That asymmetry is the point: four of the five are files, and a file tells you nothing once it leaves your phone.

## When people actually do this: 49.4% on the day itself

SubhSandesh measured one festival properly. Across both rakhi page collections, **n = 89** pages, comparing build date to festival date in IST calendar days: **49.4%** were built on the day itself, **27.0%** the day before, and **86.1%** of those finished in time landed within 24 hours. Median lead time was **0 days**, and not one of the 89 was built more than seven days ahead.

Two things must be said plainly. First, it is **Raksha Bandhan, not Ganesh Chaturthi** — a different festival, and a one-day one, where Ganesh Chaturthi runs from 14 to 25 September 2026. The shape is suggestive, not measured for this festival.

Second, **n = 89 is small**: it will not support a per-template or per-region rate, and cannot project a count of Ganesh pages.

The practical reading survives both caveats. Pages competing for this query address someone browsing at leisure in August; the only festival this platform measured says the reader arrives on the morning itself and finishes in one sitting — median **5.4 hours** from first save to last edit. Which is the case for the sticker: on the morning, it fits the time you have.

## When a sticker is right: 144 of 3,894 pages are occasion-dated

Be honest about what a sticker beats. In a group of forty relatives at 7 a.m. a sticker is correct and a link is not: it acknowledges everyone at once, costs nobody a tap, and closes the thread.

Griggio and colleagues, in a CSCW study of fifteen heavy messaging-app users, found people customise apps ["to express their identities, organizational culture, and intimate bonds with others"](https://hal.science/hal-02295535), then hit "expression breakdowns" moving that expression between apps. A sticker pack is the low-friction end of that spectrum. Only its abstract was readable from here.

Be honest about the platform too. Occasion-dated pages — festivals plus every wedding type — are **144 of 3,894, 3.7%**; the other 96.3% are romantic pages. The Ganesh template went live days before the festival, so there is no page-creation history to quote yet.

A third case where a page loses: **42.0%** of creators password-protect a page before sharing (1,636 of 3,894) — sensible for a love letter, friction on a festival morning when the recipient will not hunt for a password. Leave it off, or send a sticker. And if they are in the next room, close the app: ten days of aarti twice daily beats every format above.

## Watch the page get built

Ninety seconds, start to finish — the aarti going round, the five offerings, and the box at the end where they write a line back to you: [Ganesh Chaturthi Wishes Online — Full Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpWiv5T59QY). More page walkthroughs on Instagram: [@subhsandesh_official](https://www.instagram.com/subhsandesh_official).

## Sources

- WhatsApp, "Android Stickers Apps for WhatsApp", `WhatsApp/stickers` repository README — last updated 17 April 2025; source of every format figure above.
- Ashley R. Dainas, "A CMDA Approach to Studying Graphicons", *Language@Internet* 22 (2024), article 2 — open access.
- Esther Linares Bernabéu and Francisco Yus, "A pragmatic typology of WhatsApp sticker functions", *Pragmatics*, 15 December 2025 — **abstract only was readable**.
- Dyea Dolot and Arlene Opina, "Forms and Functions of Graphicons in Facebook Private Conversations Among Young Filipino Users", *IJLLT* 4(6), June 2021 — open access.
- Carla Griggio, Joanna McGrenere and Wendy Mackay, "Customizations and Expression Breakdowns in Ecosystems of Communication Apps", *PACM HCI* 3 (CSCW), November 2019 — **abstract only was readable**.

Two research caveats worth stating: the SERP was captured with WebSearch, which is US-localised rather than gl=in, and it does not expose whether Google serves an AI Overview for this query, so the AI Overview status is unverified in either direction.
